title: High-Protein Seitan Sheet Pan Eggs
description: A lean, make-ahead egg bake with crispy homemade seitan and extra egg whites, cut into squares for dinner or grab-and-go breakfasts all week.
ingredients: 300 g homemade seitan, thawed and crumbled or diced small
5 frozen spinach balls (1 oz / 28 g each, about 140 g total)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 18×13-inch half-sheet pan with parchment, letting it come up the sides.
Thaw the 5 frozen spinach balls in a bowl in the microwave for 30–60 seconds, then squeeze out as much water as possible with your hands or a clean tea towel.
Heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add the 300 g seitan and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and crisp at the edges, about 6 minutes.

Add the diced onion and diced bell pepper to the skillet and cook until softened, about 4 minutes. Stir in the squeezed spinach and cook 1–2 minutes, breaking up clumps and cooking off any remaining moisture.
In a large bowl, whisk the 8 eggs, 2 cups (480 ml) egg whites, 1/2 tsp black pepper, and 1/4 tsp salt (if using) until smooth with no streaks of white.
Spread the seitan and vegetable mixture evenly across the lined pan, then pour the egg mixture over the top, nudging the fillings so they're evenly distributed.
Bake for 20–24 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until the center is just set and no longer jiggles. Start checking at 20 minutes, since egg-white-heavy bakes turn rubbery quickly.
Let rest for 5 minutes to firm up, then cut into 8 squares.
notes: Macros are per square (1/8 of the pan) and assume the homemade seitan batch weighs about 1,200 g cooked; each 10 g of seitan adds or removes about 2.4 g protein. The seitan is well seasoned, so taste before adding salt. Adding 1 cup shredded cheddar before baking brings each square to about 240 calories and 25 g protein. The raw whisked egg and white mixture freezes well on its own (without the fillings); thaw overnight in the fridge and re-whisk before baking. Baked squares keep 4 days in the fridge or 2–3 months frozen, wrapped individually; microwave 45–60 seconds from chilled or 1.5–2 minutes from frozen.
